MinilibX Python API

MinilibX is a small graphics library for creating windows, drawing pixels and images, and handling basic input. The mlx Python package provides a thin ctypes wrapper around the native library.

These pages describe the Python interface. The wrapper follows the C API names from mlx.h while adapting pointer output arguments to Python return values.

Quick example

This example opens a window, draws a pixel, and exits the event loop when a key is released:

from mlx import Mlx

mlx = Mlx()
mlx_ptr = mlx.mlx_init()
if mlx_ptr is None:
    raise RuntimeError("Could not connect to the display")

win_ptr = mlx.mlx_new_window(mlx_ptr, 320, 200, "MinilibX")
if win_ptr is None:
    mlx.mlx_release(mlx_ptr)
    raise RuntimeError("Could not create a window")

# On little-endian systems, colors use the integer form 0xAARRGGBB.
mlx.mlx_pixel_put(mlx_ptr, win_ptr, 160, 100, 0xFFFF0000)

def stop_on_key_release(keycode, _state):
    mlx.mlx_loop_exit(mlx_ptr)

mlx.mlx_key_hook(win_ptr, stop_on_key_release, None)
mlx.mlx_loop(mlx_ptr)

mlx.mlx_destroy_window(mlx_ptr, win_ptr)
mlx.mlx_release(mlx_ptr)

The key hook runs when a key is released. Its keycode is backend and keyboard-layout dependent; this example exits on any key release.

Note

Mlx() loads the native shared library shipped with the Python package. Build and install the package for your platform before creating an Mlx instance. See Getting started.
